headline: Time is constant, but our experience of it expands and contracts based on attention and novelty
universal_truth: Time passes at the same rate—it's our attention that speeds or slows
fun_facts: Time seems to speed up as we age because fewer experiences are novel enough to form distinct memories
Fear stretches time—the brain processes more information during threatening situations
The 'watched pot' effect is real: focusing on time passing makes it feel slower
discussion_questions: When does time fly for you? When does it crawl?
How could you make this year feel longer and richer?
What would change if you had only one year left?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Remember how summer vacation felt endless as a child? Now years vanish in a blur. Time hasn't changed—something in you has. Today, we explore why time stretches and shrinks, and how to get more life into your years.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: A 5-minute wait at the DMV feels eternal. Five hours with someone you love disappears instantly. Same minutes, vastly different experiences. What determines whether time drags or flies?
cliff.prompt: What makes time feel faster or slower?

options.text: Novelty and attention—routine speeds time, new experiences slow it
options.response: Exactly. Your brain encodes more when things are new, making time feel fuller.

options.text: Enjoyment—fun things go fast, boring things go slow
options.response: Enjoyment matters, but the mechanism is more specific...

q1.title: The Novelty Factor
q1.script: Children experience constant novelty—every day brings new information. Adults live in routine—same commute, same tasks. Your brain doesn't bother encoding routine, so fewer memories form. Fewer memories mean time seems faster in retrospect.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Novelty Factor"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Fear Expands Time
q2.script: During accidents or threats, people report time slowing dramatically. Research shows the brain processes more information per second during danger. Time doesn't actually slow—you just notice more, making the moment feel longer.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Watched Pot
q3.script: Focusing on time passing makes it feel slower—that's why waiting is torture. When you're absorbed in something, time disappears. This is why 'flow state' activities seem to compress hours into minutes. Attention determines duration.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Want more life? Seek novelty. Try new things, go new places, break routines. Your brain will encode more, and looking back, your life will feel longer and richer. Routine is the thief of time.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 29. Tomorrow, we'll explore why everything changes—the final lesson of January. Until then, do one thing differently than usual. Give your brain something new to encode.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Time Expansion - Introduce Novelty
growTrack.learning_objective: Slow down subjective time through new experiences
growTrack.activity: Do one thing today that breaks your routine—take a different route, try a new food, have a conversation with someone new. Pay attention to details. Notice if the day feels slightly longer in retrospect.
